title: kbext.py rehearse takes a planted fork and a group overlay from one upstream ext tag to the next and reports no conflict, no shipped file edited and every extender verified
goal: kbext.py rehearse --upstream URL --from TAG --to TAG --team DIR [--fork] works in temporary directories it removes; it clones the upstream at the first tag with the group's settings and with --fork a planted fork commit adding a group root by kbroot.py add; it takes the second tag with kbgit.py upstream; it prints the conflicting paths, the shipped files the group's setup changed and kbext.py verify's lines; it exits 0 only when there is no conflict, no shipped file changed and every extender verified; --plant builds the upstream from the running checkout's tracked tools as two commits tagged ext-v<API_VERSION> and the next minor; --plant --break makes the second commit remove the ranker point without a major version, which rehearse reports by name with exit 1

clauses.clause: kbext.py rehearse --upstream URL --from TAG --to TAG --team DIR [--fork] works in temporary directories it removes

gates.question: How does rehearse let kbgit.py upstream take the second tag, which kbgit.py fetches only as main of the upstream remote?
options: A bare copy of the upstream whose main is moved from the first tag to the second
Change kbgit.py upstream to take a --ref tag
gates.recommendation: A bare copy of the upstream whose main is moved from the first tag to the second
gates.reason: the clone's own kbgit.py upstream runs unchanged, as a group runs it
gates.answer: A bare copy of the upstream whose main is moved from the first tag to the second

gates.question: How do the group's settings reach the rehearsal clone, and which changed files count as shipped?
options: KB_GROUP_SETTINGS names the team's settings file, and a shipped file is one tracked at the first tag that the group's setup modified or deleted
A settings.json is written into the clone naming the team's file, and every changed path counts
gates.recommendation: KB_GROUP_SETTINGS names the team's settings file, and a shipped file is one tracked at the first tag that the group's setup modified or deleted
gates.reason: the clone's tree stays the group's real setup, and files the group only adds are its own
gates.answer: KB_GROUP_SETTINGS names the team's settings file, and a shipped file is one tracked at the first tag that the group's setup modified or deleted

gates.question: What does the planted upstream hold, and which exit codes does rehearse use?

Every tracked file of the checkout, and exit 1 for every failure
